name: Kiss curl

lead: A kiss curl, also called a spit curl, is a lock of hair curled and pressed flat against the face, usually on the forehead or temple. It works as a small accent that frames the face and draws attention to the brow and cheek area.

The style dates to fringes of curls fashionable in the late 1600s, and in the 20th century both men and women wore it. Notable wearers include Bill Haley, Josephine Baker and the character Superman. No research tests its effect on attractiveness; it is documented through fashion history and styling practice.

paras: A thin section of hair at the front hairline is dampened, twisted around a finger or small curler, flattened against the skin and set with gel, pomade or, traditionally, saliva, sometimes with a pin until dry. On curly hair, baby hairs or edges can be shaped into the curl. It generally needs to be redone each day.

There are no known health risks beyond those of styling products and heat tools, such as scalp irritation or heat damage. Frequent tight styling of the same hairline strands can stress hair, and the curl typically loses its shape in humidity or sweat.

lead: A kiss curl, also called a spit curl, is a lock of hair curled flatly onto the face [1]. It is usually set against the forehead, temple or cheek and held with gel, pomade or traditionally saliva [2].

As a look, it is used to frame the face and add a vintage or sculpted accent. Wikipedia notes late-17th-century fringes of curls known as fripons or guigne-galants, and that in the 20th century both men and women wore the style [1]. Singer Bill Haley wore a large curl over his right eye, which reportedly drew attention away from his blind left eye; Josephine Baker, Diana Ross and Superman are also associated with it [1]. The 1990s 'laid edges' style was inspired by it [1].
Grokipedia describes a revival of the style at the 2025 Met Gala, where several celebrities wore versions of it [2]. No research has examined its effect on perceived attractiveness.

paras: The curl is plastered flat against the face. The name 'spit curl' comes from flattening with saliva, but soap or hair lotion is more typical [1]. Grokipedia gives the earliest recorded use of 'kiss curl' as an 1856 issue of Punch [2].

A thin section of hair is selected at the hairline, dampened, wrapped around a finger or small curler, and set with gel or pomade, then left to dry or pinned [2]. On straight hair a small curling iron can be used; on curly hair, natural baby hairs can be shaped; reapplying product and reshaping each morning is described as the usual upkeep [2].

In the late 1600s, curled fringes called fripons, guigne-galants or kiss-curls were fashionable [1]. In the 20th century, men and women wore the style, and Bill Haley, Josephine Baker, Diana Ross and the fictional Superman are cited as wearers [1]. The 1990s laid-edges style was inspired by it [1].
